title: Weekly Park Visits Help Kids Both Socially and Emotionally
paragraphs: Taking children to a park at least once a week can help both their social and emotional development, according to a new study from the University of Exeter in the UK.
The study used data from over 4,000 children who took part in the UK's Children of the 90s study, which has followed children's development from the early 1990s to the present day.
Data on problems with the children's behavior, emotions and ability to form relationships with others was collected in surveys at five points between the ages of 4 and 11.

Looking at the data, the researchers found that children who were taken to the park at least once a week at every age had fewer social, emotional and behavioral problems than those who went less than once a week.
For children who went to parks more at some ages and less at others, it was also found that they had fewer problems during the times when they went to parks more.
The researchers said parks may help children's social and emotional development by giving them chances to enjoy physical activity, play with other children, and have time with their parents.
Perhaps unsurprisingly, children generally went to parks more when they were younger, and less as they got older.

But at young ages, children from richer families were taken to parks more often than children from poorer families. Then, as they got older, children from poorer families started to go to parks a little more often than those in richer families.

The researchers suggest that this may be because richer parents are better able to take time off work and go to parks together when their children are younger. And while richer parents can pay for other activities as their children get older, poorer families continue to use parks longer because they're free.
